subject: Making awkward kitchen spaces useful
hook: The blind corner is where saucepans go to disappear. One detail fixes that.
ig:
The blind corner is where saucepans go to disappear. One detail fixes that.

Where two runs of kitchen units meet, one cupboard ends up with a deep, dark space behind its neighbour. With a plain shelf, the back of it is only reachable on your knees with a torch.

A pull-out corner fitting changes how that space works. Instead of reaching in, the storage comes out to you:

- Everything is visible at once, so nothing gets forgotten at the back.
- Heavy pans don't need lifting over other items.
- The full depth of the corner is used, not just the front half.

The alternative some people prefer is to blank the corner off and put deep drawers on either side. That's a genuine option too, and we'll talk through both when planning.

Which detail matters most in your kitchen: corners, drawers or tall storage? Tell us below.
fb:
We all know a corner cupboard like this: the one where the slow cooker lives and nobody can reach it.

In a bespoke kitchen, that corner can be fitted with pull-out storage that brings everything forward when you open the door. No kneeling, no torch, no forgotten tins at the back.

It's one of the most common requests when we plan kitchens around here, and it's a small change that makes a kitchen far easier to live with. Does your kitchen have a corner like this?
